newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Discovery Channel moves out of Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Discovery Channel moves out of Hong Kong.

text.p: Cable television's Discovery Channel has moved its regional headquarters from Hong Kong to Singapore to save money, its owners said on Thursday.
Kevin-John McIntyre, Senior Vice President of privately-owned Discovery Inc, said the move had nothing to do with the British colony's return to China at the end of June 1997.
"It simply was not a consideration," he told reporters. "The decision to relocate was made purely on the basis of economic consolidation."

Discovery Channel moved its administrative, financial and marketing departments -- 16 people -- to Singapore last month to join broadcast and technical staff who have been in Singapore since the channel started up in Asia in January 1994.

"Our move to Singapore makes perfect business sense. As the Republic grows into the media hub of Asia, Discovery Channel will be able to take advantage of the excellent technical and communications infrastructure here," McIntyre said.

He said the documentary and educational cable network was the anchor client of Singapore's Asia Broadcast Centre, a privately-built centre for broadcasters which MacIntyre described as one of the most advanced in the world.
He said Discovery Channel would maintain a presence in Hong Kong, concentrating on China operations.
"China is an amazing market. We are doing a lot of business in China," he said.
Launched in the United States in 1985, the Discovery Channel reaches 145 countries and broadcasts in 17 languages, he said.
